scope: Root-cause record for the earlier omnilingual browser failure.
conclusion: The int8 graph and the WebGPU provider are both correct. The failure came from the probe feeding jfk-short.wav, which is out of domain for this model.
evidence: PCM digest proved the browser audio path was also wrong: the default browser-target-rate strategy round-trips through AudioContext and produced 584bb2fe... while Node produced ebd52851... for the same file. Switching the probe to native-rate made the digests identical.
With identical PCM, the Node decode of the same int8 graph still produced garbage on jfk-short, so the graph was never the cause.
On the model own fixture tools/data/fixtures/audio/omnilingual/en.wav, the Node greedy decode returns "ask not what your country can do for you ask what you can do for your country".
The browser WebGPU run on that same fixture reports status pass and baselineMatch true with the same text.
correction_to_earlier_record: An earlier note said Node passed while the browser failed. Those runs used different fixtures: the Node passes were on the four shipped language clips, the browser failure was on jfk-short. The comparison was never fixture-matched.
probe_fixes: src/ctc-asr-webgpu.js reports audio.pcmSha256, so a decode difference cannot be mistaken for a graph difference.
The probe decodes with strategy native-rate and therefore parses the WAV directly.
The probe accepts an absolute or root-relative audio path for custom fixtures.
remaining_limits: The model does not transcribe jfk-short. It is a 1600+ language CTC model and that fixture is outside its demonstrated domain. Do not read a jfk-short result as a quality signal for it.
fp32 self-export stays blocked on the omnilingual-asr install plus the 1.3 GB checkpoint.
